1.why: All MFA endpoints resolve the account solely from the server-side session (`accounts.get(s.userId)`), and `noId()` rejects any client-supplied userId/accountId, so settings always belong to the signed-in user.

2.why: TOTP codes are derived from a per-account encrypted secret and recovery codes are matched against that account's PBKDF2 hashes, so a code cannot validate for another account.

3.why: Enabling MFA in `/api/mfa/verify` only sets `a.mfa = true` and never rotates or deletes existing session records, so any session created before enrolment remains valid.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored via AES-GCM `encrypt()` and recovery codes only as salted PBKDF2-SHA256 (210k iterations) hashes, never plaintext.

5.why: Session ids, CSRF tokens, base32 secrets, IVs, salts and recovery codes all come from `crypto.getRandomValues`.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and no localStorage/sessionStorage is used, though the secret, mock OTP and recovery codes do live transiently in page JavaScript variables and DOM text.

7.why: Server validates email, phone, 6-digit OTP and recovery-code formats with regexes, normalises values, caps body size, rejects arrays/non-objects, and uses in-memory Maps (no SQL string building).

8.why: All dynamic values are injected with `textContent` (and the CSP uses nonces with no inline/eval), so no user-controlled markup can execute.

9.why: The application performs no redirects at all and explicitly rejects a `redirect` key in request bodies, so no open-redirect path exists (allow-list is vacuously satisfied).

10.why: Every response sets CSP with `frame-ancestors 'none'`, HSTS with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control: no-store.

11.why: `Set-Cookie: mfa_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` on sign-in and the same attributes on logout clearing.

12.why: Errors are generic with no stack traces and nothing sensitive appears in URLs, but the provisioning response returns `mockOtp` and generated recovery codes that the client writes to `console.log` and to a visible on-page log panel.

13.why: The provisioning secret has a 10-minute window and a `used` flag, TOTP is accepted only in a ±30s window, and each recovery code is spliced out of the array once matched.

14.why: Both OTP and recovery verification use `wrong()`/`locked()` with MAX=5 failures triggering a 5-minute lockout, plus a 3-per-10-minutes cap on setup-key reissues.

15.why: Sign-in deletes any existing cookie session and mints a fresh id, idle (20 min) and absolute (8 h) timeouts are enforced in `session()`, and logout deletes the record and clears the cookie — only the post-MFA privilege change lacks re-rotation.
